q: Which gym zone should generally stay within view of the attendants' or front-desk station?
n: Free weights and bench press stations carry the highest risk of injury from dropped or mishandled equipment and improper form, so this area is typically kept in direct sightline of staff at the front desk for supervision and quick response.

q: Which anthropometric measurement governs the placement height of signage and the heights of privacy screens or partitions?
n: Sightline-related design decisions — where signage should sit to be read comfortably, and how tall a screen or partition needs to be to block or preserve a line of sight — are governed by eye height, since that's the point from which the person actually views the space.

q: Under which classification does a building's transformer room fall?
n: A transformer room houses electrical infrastructure equipment, which places it under utilities — the classification for the systems that supply power, water, and similar essential infrastructure to a building.

q: Which body measurement should guide seating allowances at tables and in rows within theaters and auditoriums?
n: The width each seated person occupies side-to-side is set by shoulder breadth, which is why it's the governing dimension for how much lateral space to allow per seat in a row or at a shared table.

q: What term names features whose sole purpose is user comfort and enjoyment, and raising a site's or building's appeal or value?
n: Amenities are the extra, non-essential features — pools, landscaped courts, decorative elements — that exist to please users and boost a property's appeal or market value, rather than to serve an operational or infrastructural need.

q: Which applied discipline designs and arranges tools, equipment, and spaces for the safest, most efficient human use?
n: Ergonomics is the applied science of fitting the designed environment — tools, furniture, workstations — to the user, so that the interaction between person and object is safe and efficient; anthropometry (body measurement) is one of the inputs ergonomics relies on, but the discipline itself is broader.

q: What term names the maximum horizontal span measured across the deltoid muscles?
n: Shoulder breadth is defined as the widest horizontal measurement across the deltoids, distinguishing it from elbow-to-elbow breadth (which is typically wider, taken with arms slightly out) and from body depth measurements (which are front-to-back, not side-to-side).

q: Under which classification does a music-choreographed LED fountain feature fall?
n: A music-synchronized light fountain exists purely to delight users and elevate the perceived value of the development — it serves no operational or infrastructural function, which is the hallmark of an amenity.

q: Per Time-Saver Standards, what is the maximum recommended vertical viewing angle used to set the minimum front-row-to-screen distance in a cinema?
n: The Time-Saver Standards set 33 degrees as the maximum vertical viewing angle for the front-row seat, since beyond that angle a viewer sitting too close has to tilt their head back excessively to take in the top of the screen — this angle is what sets the minimum front-row-to-screen distance (Source: Time-Saver Standards for Building Types).

q: Which term(s) refer to the maximum ground area of a lot a building's footprint may cover?
n: Both PSOmax (maximum percentage of site occupancy) and AMBF (allowable maximum building footprint) describe the same ceiling on how much of the lot's ground area the building may occupy — they're two labels for the maximum footprint concept, so both apply.

q: Which flooring material suits the common/general-use areas of an elderly residential facility?
n: Vinyl flooring offers slip resistance, a smooth (non-catching) surface for walkers and wheelchairs, and easier maintenance than carpet, while avoiding the slip hazard of glossy tile and the abrasiveness/unevenness of rough cement — making it a common choice for elder-care common areas.

q: What is the horizontal distance from the rearmost point of the buttocks to the back of the knee called?
n: Buttock-popliteal length is precisely this seated horizontal measurement, and it is a key dimension used to size seat depth so a chair supports the thighs without pressing into the back of the knee.

q: Per the NHA's site-selection standards, what density ceiling, in units per hectare, applies to two-storey low-rise residential buildings?
n: For vertical, low-rise residential development of two storeys, the NHA's site development standards cap density at 192 dwelling units per hectare — higher than the cap set for horizontal (row house) schemes because stacking units on the same footprint yields more units per unit of land (Source: NHA site selection/site development standards).

q: Which term names the combined total of a building's maximum allowable footprint and its maximum allowable paved open space?
n: MACA (maximum allowable construction area, or similarly defined hardscape ceiling) is the sum of the building's maximum footprint plus the maximum area of paved open space permitted on the lot — combining the building coverage limit with the hardscaped-yard coverage limit into one figure.

q: Which term covers measuring a person's capacity for tasks like reaching, moving, and maneuvering, along with how they use surrounding space and equipment?
n: Functional anthropometry looks at body dimensions in the context of movement and task performance — not fixed body measurements alone (that's static anthropometry) — which makes it the relevant measure for how people actually reach, maneuver, and interact with space and equipment.

q: Under which classification does an on-site sewage treatment plant fall?
n: A sewage treatment plant is infrastructure that processes and manages wastewater for the development, which places it squarely under utilities alongside power and water systems.

q: What efficiency ratio (net usable area against gross floor area) is typically acceptable for an office building?
n: Office buildings are generally planned so that around 85% of the gross floor area is leasable or usable space, with the remainder given to circulation, cores, and building services, per standard office space-planning efficiency benchmarks.

q: On a sloping lot, orienting the building pad's long dimension which way tends to produce taller retaining walls?
o: Perpendicular to (cutting across) the contour lines
n: When the pad's long side cuts across (runs against) the contour lines, it spans a greater range of elevation change along its length, forcing the retaining structure to hold back more soil height. Orienting the long side parallel to the contours instead keeps the pad closer to a single elevation and keeps retaining walls lower.

q: Under which classification does an on-site daycare center fall?
n: A daycare is a dedicated space built to support a specific activity or user need, which is what defines a facility — distinct from an amenity (comfort/enjoyment feature) or a utility (infrastructure system).

q: Which term names provisions that support a function, enable building operations, and speed up movement into, out of, and around a site while staying comfortable for users?
n: Services covers operational, movement-facilitating provisions — things like circulation systems, drop-offs, and access points — distinct from amenities (comfort/enjoyment features), facilities (spaces for specific activities), and utilities (infrastructure such as power and water).
